newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Political tension shadows Bangladesh anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Political tension shadows Bangladesh anniversary.

text.p: Bangladesh went ahead on Saturday with preparations for a star-studded independence anniversary celebration next week despite a looming nationwide general strike which poses a major challenge to the government.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina left for Pakistan on Saturday to attend a one-day summit of the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC).
Back at home, the government kicked off a dress rehearsal for Wednesday's independence celebrations with a rally by leading entertainers and other celebrities.

Hasina, who took office last June, faces a major test on Sunday in the eight-hour national strike called by the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
Khaleda has urged Bangladeshis to join in the strike as a way of helping to topple what she called the "repressive, pro-Indian rule" of Hasina's political party, the Awami League.

The country's 26th independence anniversary on Wednesday is expected to be attended by South African President Nelson Mandela, Turkish President Suleyman Demirel and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, officials said on Saturday.
The visiting dignitaries are expected to be with Hasina at the receiving ceremony.
"We are expecting a star-studded anniversary," one official told Reuters. "But the BNP-led strike is causing some worry," he said.
Police said they had been asked by authorities not to handle strikers too harshly.
Hasina on Friday asked Awami League leaders and workers to stay calm and go ahead with preparations for the celebrations.
